props.description: Watch runs, answer the ones that need you, resume or stop them, read what they produced, and hand classes of questions to your own handler workflows.

text.insert: A run ends in one of three ways: it finishes, it fails, or it pauses because it needs something from outside. This page covers what you do with each: see what is running, answer the runs that wait for you, resume or stop a run, and read what a finished run left behind. The second half is the JSON contract for scripts and agents that work the queue for you.

Copy the command the item prints, or write it yourself:

archon workflow respond <run-id> <choice> "why"                # any declared choice
archon workflow approve <run-id> "Looks good"
archon workflow reject <run-id> --reason "Not this week"
archon workflow answer <run-id> --occurrence <id> --choose use-dev

In a terminal, an answer continues the run in place. With

Resume, cancel or abandon a run

archon workflow resume <run-id>       # rerun a failed or paused run, skipping completed nodes
archon workflow resume <run-id> --detach
archon workflow end-turn <run-id>     # end a running run's stalled turn
archon workflow cancel <run-id>       # stop a running run
archon workflow abandon <run-id>      # give up on a run for good
Pick the command by what is wrong:
A turn is stuck, but the run should go on.

run. It stops the process that owns the run, confirms it stopped, and then records

A sub-run whose execution owner cannot be accounted for retains its checkout with a cleanup warning; cancellation still succeeds. See the

Stages hand each other files in
, so the artifacts are usually where the answer is: a report, a plan, a review. They live under

Hand a class of questions to a workflow
Archon routes nothing: every answerer sees every item. Labels are how your own handler workflows find the items they own. A
node can label its pause, with values that may reference earlier nodes:

- id: ask
    depends_on: [classify]
    wait:
      attention: "$classify.output.summary"
      form: select
      options: [{ id: retry }, { id: stop }]
      labels:
        ci: "$classify.output.cause"     # e.g. "pr" or "other"
        area: delivery
Labels are a flat map from string to string. A key is one token with no
or whitespace. Only attention waits carry labels; a gate's item has none. To see which classes recur often enough to deserve a handler, count them:
This handler answers delivery runs whose CI went red for a reason outside the change, labelled

name: ci-other-handler
description: Retry or stop delivery runs paused on CI failures the change did not cause
nodes:
  - id: queue
    bash: archon workflow attention --json --all --label ci=other
  - id: decide
    depends_on: [queue]
    prompt: |
      Each item in this queue is a delivery run paused because CI failed for a reason
      outside the change. For every item, read its transcript (context.transcript) and
      decide whether retrying can succeed.

      $queue.output
    output_format:
      type: object
      properties:
        answers:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            properties:
              runId: { type: string }
              occurrence: { type: string }
              option: { type: string, enum: [retry, stop] }
            required: [runId, occurrence, option]
      required: [answers]
  - id: answer
    depends_on: [decide]
    bash: |
      answers=$decide.output.answers
      items=$(printf '%s' "$answers" | jq -c '.[]') || exit 1
      if [ -z "$items" ]; then
        exit 0
      fi
      failed=0
      while read -r item; do
        if ! result=$(archon workflow respond "$(jq -r .runId <<<"$item")" "$(jq -r .option <<<"$item")" \
          --occurrence "$(jq -r .occurrence <<<"$item")" --json); then
          printf '%s\n' "$result" >&2
          failed=1
          continue
        fi
        if ! printf '%s\n' "$result" | jq -e '.ok == true' >/dev/null; then
          printf '%s\n' "$result" >&2
          failed=1
        fi
      done <<<"$items"
      exit "$failed"
An answer command exits non-zero when the answer is refused, including with

). An answer accepted while the run's resource is full exits 0: the run keeps its place and a continuation host continues it when a slot frees. If two handlers watch the same class, the occurrence check refuses the second answer.
A handler can also classify instead of answer. A cheap classifier lists the
label, asks a small model for a typed class, urgency and whether an agent can answer, and writes the result back:

archon workflow attention label <run-id> --occurrence <occurrence> \
  --set class=ci-other --set urgency=high --set answerable=agent --json
The write merges: a key it sets replaces that key, a key it unsets is removed, and nothing else changes. A second handler then selects its class with
. The labels are yours. Archon never reads
, and never decides whether a person or an agent answers.

text.insert: . Each child pauses at its own attention wait, with its own question, choices and occurrence. A parent blocked on its children is never an item, and reading the parent returns only its first actionable descendant. To find every question, list the queue and select the items whose

archon workflow attention --json --all
archon workflow answer <child-run-id> --occurrence <occurrence> --choose accept
Answer the children in any order. Each child applies its own answer at once. The parent stays paused until every child finishes, then reads their ordered results.
